subject.name: Global Politics
subject.programme: IB DP Global Politics SL/HL (first exam 2026)
subject.examPattern: IB DP – graded 1–7; recommended 150 h SL / 240 h HL; exams May (Hindi May only). HL: Paper 1 source-based 1 h 15 (20%) – 4 sources, 4 questions; Paper 2 extended response 1 h 30 (30%) – 2 essays; Paper 3 HL 1 h 30 (30%) – 3 stimulus-based questions on challenges; IA engagement project (20%). Paper marks UNVERIFIED.

items.name: Introduction to Global Politics: Political Issues, Actors and Levels of Analysis
Core: Power – Nature, Forms and Distribution
Core: Interdependence – Global Governance and Cooperation
Thematic Study: Rights and Justice – Nature and Evolution of Human Rights
Rights and Justice – Codification, Protection and Monitoring
Rights and Justice – Debates: Universalism, Relativism and Justice
Thematic Study: Development and Sustainability – Contested Meanings of Development
Development and Sustainability – Factors, Pathways and Actors
Development and Sustainability – Sustainability, Environment and Debates
Paper 1 Source Analysis and Paper 2 Extended Response Skills

subtopics.name: What is a political issue? Identifying global political issues in local, national, international and global contexts
subtopics.prerequisiteNote: Governance and political systems (MYP 5 I&S); reading current affairs news

subtopics.name: State and non-state actors: IGOs, NGOs, MNCs, social movements and individuals
subtopics.prerequisiteNote: Role of the UN and international organisations (MYP 5 Governance unit)

subtopics.name: Key concepts of the course: power, sovereignty, legitimacy, interdependence, rights, justice, liberty, equality, development, globalization, inequality, sustainability, peace, conflict, violence, non-violence
subtopics.prerequisiteNote: MYP I&S key and related concepts (global interactions, systems, power)

subtopics.name: Definitions and forms of power: hard, soft, smart, structural and relational power
subtopics.prerequisiteNote: State and non-state actors; examples of military and economic influence (MYP 5 Cold War unit)

subtopics.name: Polarity and the distribution of power: unipolar, bipolar and multipolar world orders
subtopics.prerequisiteNote: Cold War bipolar world (MYP 5); forms of power

subtopics.name: Power of non-state actors: MNCs, NGOs, terrorist groups and social media platforms
subtopics.prerequisiteNote: Forms of power; types of non-state actors

subtopics.name: Applying power to a case study: e.g. China's Belt and Road Initiative
subtopics.prerequisiteNote: Forms of power; polarity; map reading of trade routes

subtopics.name: Sovereignty: Westphalian, internal and external, de jure and de facto
subtopics.prerequisiteNote: State as a political actor; borders and governments (MYP 5 Governance unit)

subtopics.name: Challenges to state sovereignty: globalization, supranational bodies and humanitarian intervention
subtopics.prerequisiteNote: Sovereignty definitions; power of non-state actors; NATO in Kosovo (IB History)

subtopics.name: Contested statehood and self-determination: Taiwan, Kosovo, Palestine, Western Sahara

subtopics.name: Sources of legitimacy: Weber's traditional, charismatic and legal-rational authority
subtopics.prerequisiteNote: Sovereignty; types of government (democracy, authoritarianism) (MYP 5)

subtopics.name: Legitimacy of states and regimes: elections, performance and international recognition
subtopics.prerequisiteNote: Weber's types of authority; elections and representation (MYP 4 Rights and Democracy unit)

subtopics.name: Legitimacy of non-state actors and global institutions: UN Security Council, IMF, NGOs

subtopics.name: Interdependence and globalization: economic, political, cultural and environmental
subtopics.prerequisiteNote: Globalisation and trade (MYP 5 I&S); forms of power

subtopics.name: Global governance: the United Nations system and its main organs
subtopics.prerequisiteNote: Legitimacy of global institutions; interdependence

subtopics.name: Regional and economic cooperation: EU, ASEAN, African Union, WTO, G20
subtopics.prerequisiteNote: UN system; trade blocs (MYP 5 Globalisation unit)

subtopics.name: Limits of cooperation: collective action problems, nationalism and backlash against globalization
subtopics.prerequisiteNote: Regional cooperation; challenges to sovereignty

subtopics.name: Realism and neorealism: anarchy, security dilemma and balance of power
subtopics.prerequisiteNote: Polarity and distribution of power

subtopics.name: Liberalism and neoliberal institutionalism: cooperation, interdependence and democratic peace
subtopics.prerequisiteNote: Realism (for contrast); interdependence

subtopics.name: Constructivism: identities, norms and the social construction of politics
subtopics.prerequisiteNote: Realism and liberalism; role of ideas and identity

subtopics.name: Critical perspectives: Marxism, feminism and postcolonialism
subtopics.prerequisiteNote: Constructivism; colonialism and decolonisation (MYP 5)

subtopics.name: Defining human rights, rights and justice: natural, legal and moral rights

subtopics.name: Generations of rights: civil-political, socio-economic and collective rights

subtopics.name: Theories of justice: Rawls, utilitarianism, libertarianism and social justice

subtopics.name: Contested rights: rights of minorities, women, LGBTQ+ and Indigenous peoples

subtopics.name: Politicization of rights: selectivity, sanctions and the use of rights in foreign policy

subtopics.name: Defining development: economic growth, human development and capability approach (Sen)

subtopics.name: Debates: degrowth, green growth and the global North-South divide
